threads.subject: Resignation of a Temporary Foreign Worker under the IMP--REP-2019-3160
threads.question:
Dear Sir or Madam:
I am a lawyer duly licensed in the Province of Ontario.
In the case where an employer submits an Offer of Employment to IRCC via the Employer Portal for a work permit under the International Mobility Program (IMP) and a Temporary Foreign Worker (TFW) is subsequently issued a work permit at the Port of Entry by the CBSA (as opposed to online or via a visa office abroad by IRCC), to whom should the employer report the employee's subsequent resignation and by what mechanism? We have previously advised employers to contact the CBSA at the POE or IRCC where post where the work permit was issued. Is there functionality on the Employer Portal to update IRCC as to the departure of the TFW?
Best regards,
Lnformon
threads.answer:
Good day,
Thank you for your question.
IRCC does not require proactive notification of changes that are part of the regulatory imposed conditions on the employer, such as wages, working conditions, location, etc-this includes terminations of employment.
However, the employer must keep all documents pertaining to the employment of the foreign national for six years beginning on the first day of employment. If there are any changes to the information that differs from what was provided in the Offer of Employment, then the employer will (if asked) have to provide the documentation that justified the change as per subsection R203(1.1)ý.
The Voluntary Disclosure mechanism was put in place to allow employers who found themselves to be non-compliant with the conditions outlined under R203(1) to inform IRCC. Disclosure of a termination of employment would not be necessary unless the relevant provincial/territorial guidelines were not followed.
More information is available on our website at the following link: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-) citizenship/services/work-canada/hire-foreign-worker/temporary/international-mobility-program/voluntary-disclosure.html
Several conditions are imposed automatically on the employer by the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) on issuance of a work permit based on an offer of employment from that employer.
These conditions include that an employer must:
e actively engaged in the business in respect of which the offer of employment was made;
'omply with the federal and provincial laws that regulate employment, and the recruiting of employees, in the province in which the foreign national works;
rovide the foreign national with employment in the same occupation as that set out in the foreign national's offer of employment and with wages and working conditions that are substantially the same as — but not less favourable than — those set out in that offer;
nake reasonable efforts to provide a workplace that is free of abuse, within the meaning of paragraph 72.1(7)(a) if the IRPR.
The employer who provided the offer on which the work permit is based is responsible for ensuring that the foreign worker is/was provided what was stated in the Offer of Employment up until the date of termination/resignation. Employers may be inspected on these conditions and they will have to provide proof at the time of inspection that they met these conditions or
provide a justification as to why they did not.
Thank you and Happy Holidays!

threads.answer:
\cbpat2Good day,
\cbpat2
\ebpat2Question:
\cbpat2Can you please clarify whether family members of TRP-holders and open WP-holders (under R208) are eligible for open WPs as well? Or, do the family members need to hold TRPs in their own right (6 months or longer) in order to qualify for an open WP?
\cbpat2Is the family members' eligibility different for TRP-holders found to be victims of human trafficking?
\cbpat2
\cbpat2Response:
\cbpat2In order to be eligible for an open work permit under R208 (LMIA-exemption code H82), the applicant must have been issued a TRP valid for 6 months or greater and they have no other means of support. A family member of a TRP holder would not be eligible for the same open work permit if they were not issued their own TRP; they must meet the eligibility criteria by their own merit. The same applies for family members of TRP-holders found to be victims of human trafficking.
\cbpat2
\cbpat2Depending on their circumstances and the type of work, the family member may be eligible for another type of open work permit under the International Mobility Program. For example, spouses of temporary foreign workers in high-skill occupations (i.e. NOC level 0, A and B), may be eligible for an open work permit (LMIA-exemption C41). If the principal worker holds an open work permit (e.g., post-graduation work permit, working holiday work permit, TRP holders under LMIA-exemption H82), (IRCC) cannot assess the skill level based only on the open work permit, and the spouse or common-law partner applying for the C41 exemption will need to attach proof that the principal worker is employed in an occupation in skill level 0, A or B.
\cbpat2
\cbpat2The spousal applicant should submit all the supporting documents, including
- a letter from the principal foreign worker's current employer confirming employment or a copy of their employment offer or contract; and
- a copy of the principal foreign worker's last 3 pay slips

threads.answer:
Good day,
QUESTION:
Regarding film producer's LMIA-exempt work permit in Canada pursuant to R205(a), exemption C14.
Quoting from the IRCC OP Manual
QUOTE
As of February 17, 2016, foreign nationals....Regulations (RPR). Generaly, these positions are high wage and
unionized.
UNQUOTE
In my client's situation, the position in question is high wage but not/not unionized. Could you kindly advise if R205(a)/C-14 will be applicable in this situation? Under which circumstances is non-unionization acceptable to IRCC as an exception?
RESPONSE:
Your client would need to obtain a letter of no objection from a local union (in Canada where the work will be performed). The client does not necessarily have to be unionized. From our website (the link you provided in your question):
General criteria
Officers may apply the LMIA exemption code C14 to work permit applications received on or after February 17, 2016, if they are satisfied that the work essential to a TV or film production would create and maintain significant economic benefits and opportunities for Canadians and permanent residents.
The employer must submit an Offer of Employment, as per section R209.11, before a work permit application is made.
Officers should request both of the following supporting documents (if not already provided by the applicant) in support of work permit applications filed under LMIA exemption code C14:
- a letter of support from the production, which should generally contain specifications such as o the name and contact information for the production, the working title of the production, the province(s) or territory(ies) in Canada in which the production will take place and the proposed dates of production, o the name of the work permit applicant for the production, o a statement confirming that the individual and position are essential to that specific TV or film production,
migration, Refugees Inmn details of the significant economic benefit to Canada of the TV or film production, which may include ■the estimated number ofjobs for Canadians created by the production, the estimated budgetary spend in Canada at the federal, provincial or territorial level, a statement confirming that the TV or film production satisfies the criteria for federal, provincial or territorial tax credit for TV or film production, or is the recipient of federal, provincial or territorial funding for TV or film production, o the signature of a senior representative of the production o the date of signature;
- a letter from the relevant union or guild, which should generally contain specifications such as the description of the union or guild, the working title and the relevant location(s) of the TV or film production,
the name of the work permit applicant,
o a statement for the officer's consideration indicating that the union or guild is of the view that the work to be performed is subject to a collective agreement and that it has no objection to the foreign national working in the specified position for the specified company,
o the signature of a senior representative of the organization,
o the date of signature.
You can get an LMIA exemption opinion free of charge. Please see the link [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-)
citizenship/services/work-canada/hire-foreign-worker/temporary/international-mobility-workers-unit.html for more
information on how to submit a request with all the necessary information to receive an opinion letter from an officer. The email address where to send your request can be found in #6 below (highlighted for your reference). Your client would then bring all the supporting documentation noted above to show they meet the criteria for C14 along with the opinion letter to present to the border upon entry.
